status: DRAFT for review (Batch 2). Maps USDA FoodData Central NAMES (plus record attributes) of the category 'Vegetables and Vegetable Products' to candidate lexicon rows of kind vegetable. It never decides a NOVA group: FDC supplies naming evidence only; placement comes from the FAO clauses below.

clause.text: Fresh, squeezed, chilled, frozen, or dried fruit and leafy and root vegetables
clause.where: FAO 2019 (Monteiro et al.), Table 1, Group 1 examples, p. 11 (first example of the Group 1 row)
clause.basis: inference level: class-instance of vegetables; the clause names 'leafy and root vegetables'; stem, flower, bulb and fruit-vegetables (tomato, cauliflower, onion, courgette) are instances of the Group 1 definition 'edible parts of plants (fruit, seeds, leaves, stems, roots, tubers)' (same table), not named by the example
clause.scope: The clause is unconditioned and names the forms fresh, squeezed, chilled, frozen or dried. A plain raw or frozen-unprepared vegetable is an instance. Cooked, canned, pickled, salted, sauced, fried, mashed or otherwise prepared forms, vegetable products (sauce, juice, puree, chips, fries, flour, powder, dishes) and mixtures are not instances of this clause.

clauses_alt.text: starchy roots and tubers such as potatoes, sweet potatoes and cassava
clauses_alt.basis: inference level: class-instance of starchy roots and tubers (the clause names potatoes, sweet potatoes and cassava)

clauses_alt.text: fungi such as fresh or dried mushrooms
clauses_alt.basis: inference level: class-instance of fungi (the clause names fresh or dried mushrooms)

acceptance: A1. The FDC food category is exactly 'Vegetables and Vegetable Products'.

A2. The plain form is established by the name ('raw', or 'frozen' + 'unprepared', both forms the clause names) OR by the record attribute: a Foundation record whose FoodOn item name states '(raw)' where the description does not.
A3. The name holds no word from the word guard, no product word and no queue word; the head is a single food (a head naming two foods with 'and' is a mixture: QUEUE).
A4. Record attributes do not contradict the plain form (no portion descriptor holding a guard word).
A5. The derived label term is a distinct food name: else QUEUE.

A6. Canonical deduplication: cut, grade, colour-shade and cultivar variants of one food collapse into ONE row (table 'canonical' and the collapse-word rule); the rest are synonym CANDIDATES (synonyms.csv is not touched).

word_guard.why: The category-wide extension of the Spices and Herbs word guard (owner rule 3): any treatment, addition, cooking/canning liquid, product or dish word puts the name outside a plain raw or frozen-unprepared vegetable. 'baby' is NOT guarded (baby carrots are a plain cut); 'unprepared' is the clause-compatible frozen form (tokenised separately from 'prepared'); UV-exposed mushrooms (a treatment) are rejected.

product_words.why: A flour, starch or powder of a vegetable is a different form: flours belong to the flour batch; powders are food_powder candidates. REJECT here (not an instance of the fresh/frozen vegetable clause).

queue_words.sprouted: germinated seeds (sprouts) are not named by the clause; the plant-part basis is not established.
queue_words.seaweed: algae are named only in the Group 1 DEFINITION ('fungi, algae'), not in an example; kind and placement need an owner decision.
queue_words.corn: sweet corn overlaps the cereal-grain clause ('corn cob or kernel'): the Cereal batch owns it.
queue_words.immature: immature legume seeds overlap the legume rows (Batch 1).
queue_words.mature seeds: mature legume seeds belong to the legume batch.
queue_words.peas: peas and pea pods overlap the legume rows (Batch 1); the existing 'peas' row is already a legume.
queue_words.dried: dried forms: the clause names 'dried' but earlier owner policy (dehydrated-policy-1) keeps dried/dehydrated forms per-term only; QUEUE for per-term decisions.
queue_words.hearts of palm: stem of a palm: the plant-part basis is not named by the clause; QUEUE.
queue_words.fiddlehead: fern shoots: not named by the clause; QUEUE.
queue_words.lemon grass: an herb or spice (Spices and Herbs clause), not a vegetable; routed to that category's rule.
queue_words.ginger: an herb or spice (Spices and Herbs clause), not a vegetable.
queue_words.garlic: an herb or spice per FDC in other records; kept out of this batch until the owner decides garlic's class (existing label vocabulary).
queue_words.wasabi: a condiment root (Spices and Herbs clause).
queue_words.turnip greens and turnips: a mixture of two foods in one record (a head naming two foods with 'and'): not a single ingredient.
queue_words.peas and: a mixture of two foods in one record: not a single ingredient.
queue_words.flowers: an edible flower is not established as a vegetable by the clause; QUEUE.
queue_words.flower: an edible flower is not established as a vegetable by the clause; QUEUE.
